{{Short description|System of crypto-communications}}In [[telecommunications]], a '''cryptochannel''' is a complete [[system]] of [[cryptography|crypto-communications]] between two or more holders or parties. It includes: (a) the cryptographic aids prescribed; (b) the holders thereof; (c) the indicators or other means of identification; (d) the area or areas in which effective; (e) the special purpose, if any, for which provided; and (f) pertinent notes as to distribution, usage, ''etc.'' A cryptochannel is analogous to a [[radio]] [[Telecommunication circuit|circuit]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-02-09 |title=Cryptography Definition |url=https://www.kaspersky.com/resource-center/definitions/what-is-cryptography |access-date=2017-02-28 |website=www.kaspersky.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Mehta |first=Medha |date=2021-01-04 |title=Cryptology vs Cryptography: What's the Difference? |url=https://sectigostore.com/blog/cryptology-vs-cryptography-whats-the-difference/ |access-date=2017-02-28 |website=InfoSec Insights |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=cryptology |url=https://cs.lmu.edu/~ray/notes/cryptology/ |access-date=2017-02-28 |website=cs.lmu.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=How blockchain can impact the telecommunications industry |url=https://www2.deloitte.com/content/dam/Deloitte/za/Documents/technology-media-telecommunications/za_TMT_Blockchain_TelCo.pdf |access-date=2017-02-28 |website=Deloitte.com}}</ref>
